Mount Hor
HOR
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Hor; the mountain on the edge of Edom where Aaron the high priest died and was stripped of his garments.

📖 Biblical Definition

Mount Hor was a mountain on the border of the land of Edom where Aaron, the first high priest, died at the LORD's command, his sacred office passing to his son. Because Aaron, like Moses, had rebelled against the word of the LORD at the waters of Meribah, the LORD said he would not enter the promised land. At Mount Hor, in the sight of all the congregation, Moses brought Aaron and his son Eleazar up the mountain, "and Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there in the top of the mount" (Num 20:28). The whole congregation mourned for Aaron thirty days. The transfer of the priestly garments from father to son upon the mountain showed that the office continued though the man passed; the priesthood did not die with Aaron. Mount Hor stands in the dictionary as the mountain of the first high priest's death, a witness to the mortality of the Aaronic priests, who could not continue by reason of death, and so a pointer to the better and unchangeable priesthood of Christ, who, "because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood" (Heb 7:24), and ever lives to make intercession for His people.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A mountain on the edge of Edom where Aaron the high priest died and his garments passed to his son Eleazar (Num 20:22-29); a witness to the mortal Aaronic priesthood that points to the unchangeable priesthood of Christ.

MOUNT HOR, proper noun. A mountain on the border of Edom.

Where Aaron the high priest died at the LORD's command (Num 20:25-28).

Where Moses stripped Aaron's garments and put them on Eleazar his son.

Aaron barred from the land for the rebellion at Meribah.

Mourned by the congregation thirty days (Num 20:29).

📖 Key Scripture

Num 20:28 — "And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there in the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount."

Num 33:38 — "And Aaron the priest went up into mount Hor at the commandment of the LORD, and died there..."

Heb 7:23 — "And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:"

Heb 7:24 — "But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Mount Hor needs no defense from redefinition; its lesson is the mortality of the Aaronic priesthood, which points to the better, unchangeable priesthood of Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the contrast between the dying priests and the ever-living Christ. The Aaronic priests "were not suffered to continue by reason of death" (Heb 7:23); Aaron himself died on Mount Hor, his office handed to another. The dictionary holds the better priesthood of Christ, who, because He continues ever, has an unchangeable priesthood and ever lives to intercede; no successor strips His garments, for He does not die, but is a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

Office-over-man note. The transfer of the priestly garments from Aaron to Eleazar on the mountain shows that the office continued though the man passed. The dictionary holds the principle: God's appointed offices and ordinances do not depend on any one mortal servant; the priesthood, the ministry, the church itself outlive the individuals who serve them, for they rest on the purpose of God, fulfilled at last and for ever in the one Priest who never dies.
